newsitem.title: CHINA: China starts bank head office re-discount business.
newsitem.headline: China starts bank head office re-discount business.

text.p: China's central bank has significantly boosted its re-discount business with the head offices of the country's four major state banks to give it greater control over money supply, bankers said on Wednesday.
The Shanghai Securities News said on Wednesday the head office of the People's Bank of China had been buying discount papers which have not yet matured since March 1 from the four big banks.

"This is a major step in the reforms of China's finance system," said a central bank official in Beijing reached by telephone. "It is part of the central bank's plan to gradually move to using indirect means of controlling money supply."

The discount papers are commercial papers bought from state firms or enterprises at a discount rate by the four banks -- the Bank of China, the Construction Bank, the Agricultural Bank and the Industrial and Commercial Bank.
The central bank has allowed its branches to do re-discount business with branches of the big four banks since 1994, but the headquarters of the banks have never before been involved.

The central bank "can use floating re-discount rates to influence the quantity of loans supplied by the major state banks as well as market interest rates", the newspaper said. "This in turn can help it to adjust money supply at the national level."
China's money supply is mainly controlled at present through annual loan quotas from the central bank to the four big banks, which account for around 75 percent of money supply in China.
Beijing has said it will gradually abolish the administrative loan quota system and replace it with indirect means of control.
In addition to the re-discount business, it set up a local currency interbank market in early 1996 to allow state banks to lend and borrow short-term funds at market-driven rates.

In April last year, it also started open market operations trading short-term state debt with state banks as a means of giving the market a view of its direction on monetary policy including money supply.

With the rediscount business, the central bank will each year decide an annual volume for trades between its head office and other bank's head offices to create an effective means of controlling money supply, the Shanghai Securities News said.

The volume of the re-discount business conducted by the head office of any one of the major state banks with the central bank head office must not exceed half of the discount papers in its hands, it said.
The banks must supply certificates to prove the quantity of their discount papers before they can do the business, it said.
"Trading among the headquarters will greatly expand the re-discount business," said a banker with a major state bank.
"Generally speaking, we would like to sell as much of the discount paper to the central bank as possible to make our assets more liquid," she said.
Bankers said the impact of the new move was not immediately clear because there was no indication yet of the scale of the central bank's head office's re-discount business.
"The impact will mainly depend on volume of the trading among the banks' headquarters," said a banker with the Shanghai-based Communications Bank.
The newspaper said the central bank would select discount papers involving firms in pillar industries as targets of the re-discount business in order to support key sectors.
